source.label: Sirén (citing the Wusheng shi shi): Dong retired to his home province, “where he lived for eighteen years”
Waley: Dong “completely identifies the Learned Man's Painting with the Southern School”

work.text: In most of the pictures which have dated [inscriptions] from the two first decades of the seventeenth century the [decisive] influence is derived from Huang Kung-wang

source.author: Osvald Sirén
source.title: Chinese Painting: Leading Masters and Principles, vol. V (The Later Ming and Leading Ch‘ing Masters)

work.text: When I was young I imitated Huang Kung-wang’s landscapes; but in middle life I left off and copied Sung masters. Now I occasionally copy Huang again and manage a tolerable imitation.

source.author: Dong Qichang (Tung Ch‘i-ch‘ang)
source.title: Writings on painting
source.publisher: translated in Arthur Waley, An Introduction to the Study of Chinese Painting (Ernest Benn, 1923; Internet Archive scan)

moment.text: …fortunately Tung Ch'i-ch'ang arose in [Yunjian] … and his talents and eminence in Tao and art again spread glory over the peaks and gave fresh impetus to the spirit. He was indeed a man [who] opened up new paths.
moment.lead: The Ming critic Gu Ningyuan, on painting's decline late in the Wanli reign:

source.author: Gu Ningyuan (Ku Ning-yuan)
source.title: Hua yin (on Ming painters)
source.publisher: translated in Osvald Sirén, Chinese Painting: Leading Masters and Principles, vol. V (Lund Humphries, 1958; Internet Archive scan)

matters.text: He looked down on personal fame, official positions and literary accomplishments as the heron looks down on worms in the soil.

source.author: Jiang Shaoshu (Chiang Shao-shu)
source.title: Wusheng shi shi (biography of Dong Qichang)
source.publisher: translated in Osvald Sirén, Chinese Painting: Leading Masters and Principles, vol. V (Lund Humphries, 1958; Internet Archive scan)

matters.text: …after some [time] he retired from this office and settled in his home province, where he lived for eighteen years. His fame increased
